p: Sundown sits out in the countryside at Rampton, a short drive from Retford, so you'll want a car to get there. That rural setting is part of the charm: it feels like a proper day away rather than a trip to a busy retail park.

How long should you allow? Most families find it's a whole-day kind of place, mainly because little ones like to go round the same rides again and again and need regular snack stops. Arriving early gives you the calmest start and lets toddlers get their bearings before it gets busier.

Think about what your youngest will cope with. A pushchair is useful for the walk between areas, especially for tired legs after lunch, and a spare set of clothes never goes amiss with this age group. If you've got a mix of ages, let older siblings choose a favourite ride each so everyone gets a turn at being in charge of the plan.

There's lots more to do in this corner of north Nottinghamshire if you're making a weekend of it. Retford's market square is a lovely spot to browse, and the Chesterfield Canal runs right through town, ideal for a gentle stroll and a spot of duck-watching. Sherwood Forest, home of the Robin Hood legend that the park nods to, is within reach by car, so you can carry the outlaw theme on for another day. Clumber Park, with its lake, woodland and big open spaces, is another good shout for a run-around.
